source.text: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֑ים וּפַרְעֹ֣ה חֹלֵ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֖ה עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־הַיְאֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at [the] end of two years [of] days, and Pharaoh [was] dreaming, and behold, [he was] standing by the Nile.

en.L: And it happened at the end of two full years that Pharaoh dreamed, and look, he was standing by the Nile,
en.B: Two whole years later Pharaoh had a dream. He was standing beside the Nile,
en.R: After two more years had gone by, Pharaoh had a dream. He saw himself standing by the Nile River.

decisions.choice: two years of days: two full years
decisions.reason: "Years of days" means complete years. The count runs from the cupbearer's release, when he forgot Joseph (40:23); Joseph has waited in prison two more years.

decisions.choice: the River: the Nile
decisions.reason: Ye'or is a word borrowed from Egyptian for the Nile and its channels. Egypt's harvests depended on the Nile's yearly flood, so a dream that begins at the river concerns the harvests of the whole country.

decisions.choice: the Nile
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the River"; in Egypt that means the Nile, so every level names it.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִן־הַיְאֹ֗ר עֹלֹת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פָּר֔וֹת יְפ֥וֹת מַרְאֶ֖ה וּבְרִיאֹ֣ת בָּשָׂ֑ר וַתִּרְעֶ֖ינָה בָּאָֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, from the Nile [were] coming up seven cows, beautiful of appearance and fat of flesh, and they grazed among the reed[s].

en.L: and look, seven cows were coming up out of the Nile, beautiful in appearance and fat in flesh, and they grazed among the reeds.
en.B: and seven cows came climbing up out of the river, handsome and plump, and began feeding in the marsh grass.
en.R: Seven cows came up out of the river. They were fat and good-looking, and they began eating the tall grass by the water.

decisions.choice: the reeds: marsh grass along the river
decisions.reason: Achu is another word borrowed from Egyptian, for the reeds and rushes that grew in the wet ground beside the Nile, good grazing for cattle (Job 8:11 uses it of papyrus growing in the marsh).

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶׁ֧בַע פָּר֣וֹת אֲחֵר֗וֹת עֹל֤וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶן֙ מִן־הַיְאֹ֔ר רָע֥וֹת מַרְאֶ֖ה וְדַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֛דְנָה אֵ֥צֶל הַפָּר֖וֹת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, seven cows other [were] coming up after them from the Nile, bad of appearance and thin of flesh, and they stood beside the cows on [the] bank of the Nile.

en.L: And look, seven other cows were coming up after them out of the Nile, ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and they stood beside the cows on the bank of the Nile.
en.B: Then seven other cows came up from the Nile behind them, poor-looking and scrawny, and stood next to the first cows on the riverbank.
en.R: Behind them, seven other cows climbed out of the river. They were thin and ugly, and they stood next to the fat cows at the water's edge.

decisions.choice: bad in appearance: ugly, wretched-looking
decisions.reason: Ra, "bad", here describes how the cows look: poor, sickly animals, the opposite of "beautiful in appearance" in verse 2.

source.text: וַתֹּאכַ֣לְנָה הַפָּר֗וֹת רָע֤וֹת הַמַּרְאֶה֙ וְדַקֹּ֣ת הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַפָּר֔וֹת יְפֹ֥ת הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְהַבְּרִיאֹ֑ת וַיִּיקַ֖ץ פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And ate the cows, bad of appearance and thin of flesh, the seven cows, beautiful of appearance and fat. And awoke Pharaoh.

en.L: And the cows that were ugly in appearance and thin in flesh ate up the seven cows that were beautiful in appearance and fat. Then Pharaoh woke up.
en.B: And the ugly, scrawny cows devoured the seven handsome, plump ones. At that Pharaoh awoke.
en.R: Then the thin, ugly cows ate up the seven fat, good-looking ones. At that, Pharaoh woke up.

decisions.choice: the cows ate the cows: something against nature
decisions.reason: Cows do not eat meat. The strange picture is the point: the thin years will use up everything the good years produced (verses 30-31).

source.text: וַיִּישָׁ֕ן וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֖ם שֵׁנִ֑ית וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹל֛וֹת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד בְּרִיא֥וֹת וְטֹבֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he slept and dreamed a second [time], and behold, seven ears of grain [were] coming up on one stalk, fat and good.

en.L: And he fell asleep and dreamed a second time, and look, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, plump and good.
en.B: Once he was asleep again, he dreamed a second time: seven ears of grain, plump and fine, were growing up on one stalk.
en.R: Pharaoh went back to sleep and had another dream. He saw one stalk of grain with seven heads on it. The heads were plump and healthy.

decisions.choice: ears of grain: the heads of wheat or barley
decisions.reason: Shibbolet is the head of a cereal plant, where the kernels grow. Egypt grew wheat and barley (Exodus 9:31-32).

decisions.choice: heads of grain
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word "heads" for the part of the stalk that holds the grain.

source.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים דַּקּ֖וֹת וּשְׁדוּפֹ֣ת קָדִ֑ים צֹמְח֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, seven ears, thin and scorched of [the] east wind, [were] sprouting after them.

en.L: And look, seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, were sprouting up after them.
en.B: Then seven other ears came up behind them, thin and burnt dry by the east wind.
en.R: Then seven more heads of grain grew up after them. These were thin and dried up by the hot desert wind.

decisions.choice: scorched by the east wind: dried out by the hot desert wind
decisions.reason: The east wind (qadim) blows in from the desert, hot and dry, and can wither crops in a few days (Hosea 13:15; Ezekiel 17:10). In Egypt such hot winds come off the desert as well.

decisions.choice: the hot desert wind
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of wind the east wind was, since its direction alone tells a modern reader little.

source.text: וַתִּבְלַ֨עְנָה֙ הַשִּׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקּ֔וֹת אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִ֔ים הַבְּרִיא֖וֹת וְהַמְּלֵא֑וֹת וַיִּיקַ֥ץ פַּרְעֹ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֲלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And swallowed the thin ears the seven ears, the fat and the full. And awoke Pharaoh, and behold, a dream.

en.L: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven plump and full ears. Then Pharaoh woke up, and look, [it was] a dream.
en.B: And the thin ears gulped down the seven plump, full ones. Then Pharaoh woke up and found that he had been dreaming.
en.R: The seven thin heads swallowed the seven full ones. When Pharaoh woke up, he knew it was only a dream.

decisions.choice: and look, a dream: he realized it was only a dream
decisions.reason: "Look" (hinneh) lets the reader share Pharaoh's waking moment: the dream had seemed real until he woke and saw it was a dream.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ וַתִּפָּ֣עֶם רוּח֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־כָּל־חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֶת־כָּל־חֲכָמֶ֑יהָ וַיְסַפֵּ֨ר פַּרְעֹ֤ה לָהֶם֙ אֶת־חֲלֹמ֔וֹ וְאֵין־פּוֹתֵ֥ר אוֹתָ֖ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] morning, and was troubled his spirit, and he sent and summoned all [the] magicians of Egypt and all its wise [men], and recounted Pharaoh to them his dream, and there was none interpreting them for Pharaoh.

en.L: And it happened in the morning that his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them his dream, but there was no one who could interpret them for Pharaoh.
en.B: When morning came, Pharaoh was uneasy in spirit. He summoned every magician and wise man in Egypt and described his dream to them, but none of them could tell Pharaoh what it meant.
en.R: The next morning Pharaoh was upset. He sent for all of Egypt's magicians and wise men and told them his dream. But none of them could explain it to him.

decisions.choice: magicians: Egyptian priestly experts
decisions.reason: Chartummim is a title for learned Egyptian priests skilled in sacred writings, rituals and the reading of signs, including dreams. The same experts oppose Moses in Exodus 7:11, 22.

decisions.choice: his dream ... interpret them: one dream, two parts
decisions.reason: Pharaoh tells "his dream" (singular), but no one can interpret "them" (plural). The two dreams are one message, as Joseph says in verse 25.

decisions.choice: his spirit was troubled: he was disturbed and restless
decisions.reason: The verb pictures the spirit being struck or pushed about. The same is said of Nebuchadnezzar after his dream (Daniel 2:1, 3).

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֶת־חֲטָאַ֕י אֲנִ֖י מַזְכִּ֥יר הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke [the] chief of the cupbearers to Pharaoh, saying, my offenses I am bringing to remembrance today.

en.L: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, "I call to mind my offenses today.
en.B: Then the chief cupbearer spoke up and said to Pharaoh, "Today I must bring up my own faults.
en.R: Then the chief cupbearer spoke up. He said to Pharaoh, "Today I have to admit that I did wrong.

decisions.choice: the chief cupbearer: the king's wine steward
decisions.reason: The cupbearer served the king his wine and was among his most trusted officers (40:1-2, 21; Nehemiah 1:11).

decisions.choice: my offenses: his old fault, his forgetfulness, or both
decisions.reason: Chet'ay is plural. The cupbearer may mean the offense that put him in prison (40:1), or his failure to keep his promise to Joseph (40:14, 23), or both. He speaks carefully, as one reminding a king of an old grievance.

source.text: פַּרְעֹ֖ה קָצַ֣ף עַל־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתִ֜י בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֚ית שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים אֹתִ֕י וְאֵ֖ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and he put me in custody [in the] house of [the] commander of the bodyguards, me and [the] chief of the bakers.

en.L: Pharaoh was angry with his officials, and he put me in custody in the house of the commander of the guard, me and the chief baker.
en.B: There was a time when Pharaoh was angry with his officials, the chief baker and me, and he had us held in custody in the house of the commander of the guard.
en.R: Once you were angry with the chief baker and me. You put us in prison in the house of the leader of the palace guard.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh was angry: speaking to the king in the third person
decisions.reason: At court one spoke to the king as "Pharaoh" rather than "you", a mark of respect. Joseph does the same (verses 16, 25, 28).

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: Readable uses "you" when someone speaks to Pharaoh, since the third person can confuse modern readers about who is meant.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are the officers of his court, as in 40:20.

source.text: וַנַּֽחַלְמָ֥ה חֲל֛וֹם בְּלַ֥יְלָה אֶחָ֖ד אֲנִ֣י וָה֑וּא אִ֛ישׁ כְּפִתְר֥וֹן חֲלֹמ֖וֹ חָלָֽמְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he, each according to [the] interpretation of his dream we dreamed.

en.L: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream.
en.B: On the same night he and I each had a dream, and each dream carried a meaning that fit the man who dreamed it.
en.R: He and I both dreamed on the same night, and the two dreams meant different things.

decisions.choice: each according to the interpretation of his dream: each dream fit its dreamer
decisions.reason: Each man's dream matched what was going to happen to him (40:5), so the two dreams had different meanings.

source.text: וְשָׁ֨ם אִתָּ֜נוּ נַ֣עַר עִבְרִ֗י עֶ֚בֶד לְשַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים וַנְּ֨סַפֶּר־ל֔וֹוַיִּפְתָּר־לָ֖נוּ אֶת־חֲלֹמֹתֵ֑ינוּ אִ֥ישׁ כַּחֲלֹמ֖וֹ פָּתָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [there was] there with us a young man, a Hebrew, a slave of [the] commander of the bodyguards, and we recounted to him and he interpreted for us our dreams; to each according to his dream he interpreted.

en.L: And a young man was there with us, a Hebrew, a slave of the commander of the guard. And we told [them] to him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; he interpreted for each man according to his dream.
en.B: With us in custody was a young Hebrew, a slave of the commander of the guard. We described our dreams to him, and he explained them, telling each man what his own dream meant.
en.R: In prison with us was a young Hebrew, a slave who belonged to the leader of the palace guard. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each man's dream meant.

decisions.choice: a young man, a Hebrew, a slave: three marks of low standing
decisions.reason: The cupbearer describes Joseph as young, foreign and owned, someone the court would hardly take seriously. That makes what follows the more striking. "Hebrew" is what outsiders called Abraham's family (14:13; 39:14).

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּֽתַר־לָ֖נוּ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֑ה אֹתִ֛י הֵשִׁ֥יב עַל־כַּנִּ֖י וְאֹת֥וֹ תָלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, just as he interpreted to us, so it was: me he restored to my office, and him he hanged.

en.L: And it happened just as he interpreted [it] to us: I was restored to my office, and he was hanged."
en.B: Everything happened just as he said it would: Pharaoh put me back in my post, and he hanged the baker."
en.R: And it all came true, just the way he said. You gave me back my job, and the baker was hanged."

decisions.choice: he restored ... he hanged: Pharaoh, as the interpreter had said
alternatives: the interpreter restored me (by his word)
decisions.reason: Literally "me he restored ... him he hanged". The one who acted was Pharaoh (40:21-22), but the cupbearer's wording almost credits the outcome to the interpreter's word.

decisions.choice: hanged: the body put on display after execution
decisions.reason: Talah means to hang up. In 40:19 Joseph says the baker's head will be lifted off and his body hung on a pole, so this may describe exposing or impaling the body after death.

decisions.choice: I was restored ... he was hanged / Pharaoh ... the baker
alternatives: he restored me ... he hanged him
decisions.reason: Literal uses the passive to avoid an unclear "he"; Balanced names Pharaoh and the baker, and Readable uses "you" for Pharaoh.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח פַּרְעֹה֙ וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְרִיצֻ֖הוּ מִן־הַבּ֑וֹר וַיְגַלַּח֙ וַיְחַלֵּ֣ף שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Pharaoh and called Joseph, and they hurried him from the pit, and he shaved and changed his clothes, and came to Pharaoh.

en.L: So Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they hurriedly brought him out of the pit. And he shaved and changed his clothes, and came to Pharaoh.
en.B: So Pharaoh summoned Joseph, and they hurried him up out of the prison pit. Joseph shaved, put on clean clothes, and went in to Pharaoh.
en.R: Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and they rushed him out of the prison. Joseph shaved, changed into clean clothes, and went in to see Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: the pit: the prison, called by the word for a cistern
decisions.reason: Bor is the word for the cistern Joseph's brothers threw him into (37:24). Joseph used it of his prison too (40:15). He is lifted out of a pit a second time.

decisions.choice: he shaved: made ready to appear before the king
decisions.reason: Egyptian men of rank went clean-shaven, unlike men of Canaan. Joseph shaves and changes out of prison clothes to stand before Pharaoh. Again his clothing marks a turn in his life (37:23; 39:12; verse 42).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְתִּי וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַאֲנִ֗י שָׁמַ֤עְתִּי עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תִּשְׁמַ֥ע חֲל֖וֹם לִפְתֹּ֥ר אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, a dream I have dreamed and [one who] interprets it there is not; and I have heard about you, saying, you hear a dream to interpret it.

en.L: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. But I have heard it said about you that you hear a dream [and can] interpret it."
en.B: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have had a dream, and nobody can tell me what it means. Word has reached me that you only need to hear a dream to explain it."
en.R: Pharaoh told Joseph, "I have had a dream that nobody can explain. I am told that when you hear a dream, you know what it means."

decisions.choice: you hear a dream to interpret it: hearing it is enough
alternatives: you understand a dream so as to interpret it
decisions.reason: The verb "hear" can also mean "understand". Either way, Pharaoh has been told that Joseph needs only to hear a dream to give its meaning.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֛ה לֵאמֹ֖ר בִּלְעָדָ֑י אֱלֹהִ֕ים יַעֲנֶ֖ה אֶת־שְׁל֥וֹם פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Joseph Pharaoh, saying, not in me; God will answer [for] the welfare of Pharaoh.

en.L: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, "[It is] not in me. God will answer [for] the welfare of Pharaoh."
en.B: Joseph answered Pharaoh, "It is not in my power. God will give Pharaoh an answer for his good."
en.R: Joseph answered, "I cannot do it myself. But God will give you an answer that is good for you."

decisions.choice: not in me: the power belongs to God
decisions.reason: Biladay means "apart from me", "it is not up to me". Joseph refuses the credit before the king, as he did in prison: "Do not interpretations belong to God?" (40:8; compare Daniel 2:27-28).

decisions.choice: God will answer the welfare of Pharaoh: a favorable answer, an answer for his good
alternatives: God will set Pharaoh's mind at peace
decisions.reason: Shalom is well-being and peace. Joseph promises an answer that serves Pharaoh's welfare; it may also mean an answer that settles his troubled spirit (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew: "not in me; God will answer"
alternatives: "Without God no answer will be given for Pharaoh's welfare" (Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads the words differently, as "Without God". The Hebrew text is clear as it stands and is followed here.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף בַּחֲלֹמִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י עֹמֵ֖ד עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Pharaoh to Joseph, in my dream, behold, I [was] standing on [the] bank of the Nile.

en.L: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "In my dream, look, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.
en.B: So Pharaoh began to describe it to Joseph: "There I was in my dream, standing at the edge of the Nile.
en.R: Pharaoh told Joseph, "I dreamed that I was standing next to the Nile River.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִן־הַיְאֹ֗ר עֹלֹת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פָּר֔וֹת בְּרִיא֥וֹת בָּשָׂ֖ר וִיפֹ֣ת תֹּ֑אַר וַתִּרְעֶ֖ינָה בָּאָֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, from the Nile [were] coming up seven cows, fat of flesh and beautiful of form, and they grazed among the reed[s].

en.L: And look, seven cows were coming up out of the Nile, fat in flesh and beautiful in form, and they grazed among the reeds.
en.B: Up out of the river came seven cows, plump and handsome, and they fed in the marsh grass.
en.R: Seven cows, fat and good-looking, climbed out of the river and started to eat the tall grass along the bank.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶֽׁבַע־פָּר֤וֹת אֲחֵרוֹת֙ עֹל֣וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן דַּלּ֨וֹת וְרָע֥וֹת תֹּ֛אַר מְאֹ֖ד וְרַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר לֹֽא־רָאִ֧יתִי כָהֵ֛נָּה בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לָרֹֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, seven cows other [were] coming up after them, poor and bad of form very and thin of flesh; not have I seen like them in all [the] land of Egypt for badness.

en.L: And look, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly in form and thin in flesh. I have never seen [any] as ugly as them in all the land of Egypt.
en.B: Seven more cows came up behind them, weak, very ugly and all skin and bone. In all the land of Egypt I have never seen cows so bad.
en.R: Then seven other cows came up behind them. They were weak and skinny and very ugly. Nowhere in Egypt have I ever seen cows that looked so bad.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's retelling adds his own feelings
decisions.reason: Pharaoh adds details the narrator did not give in verse 3: the cows are "poor" (dallot), "very" ugly, and worse than any he has ever seen. The retelling shows how much the dream disturbed him.

source.text: וַתֹּאכַ֨לְנָה֙ הַפָּר֔וֹת הָרַקּ֖וֹת וְהָרָע֑וֹת אֵ֣ת שֶׁ֧בַע הַפָּר֛וֹת הָרִאשֹׁנ֖וֹת הַבְּרִיאֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And ate the cows, the thin and the bad, the seven cows, the first, the fat.

en.L: And the thin and ugly cows ate up the first seven cows, the fat ones.
en.B: And the lean and ugly cows devoured the first seven, the fat ones.
en.R: Then the skinny, ugly cows ate up the fat cows, all seven of them.

source.text: וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה אֶל־קִרְבֶּ֗נָה וְלֹ֤א נוֹדַע֙ כִּי־בָ֣אוּ אֶל־קִרְבֶּ֔נָה וּמַרְאֵיהֶ֣ן רַ֔ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּתְּחִלָּ֑ה וָאִיקָֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went into their insides, and not was known that they had gone into their insides, and their appearance [was] bad as at the beginning. And I awoke.

en.L: And they went into their bellies, but it could not be known that they had gone into their bellies, for they looked as ugly as at the beginning. Then I woke up.
en.B: Yet once the fat cows were inside them, nobody would have known it; they looked as wretched as they had at first. Then I awoke.
en.R: The fat cows went into their stomachs, but nobody could have guessed it. The thin cows looked as bad as they had at the start. Then I woke up.

decisions.choice: no one could tell they had eaten: the famine will swallow the plenty without a trace
decisions.reason: The picture prepares for Joseph's words in verses 30-31: the good years will be so completely used up that they will be forgotten.

source.text: וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲלֹמִ֑י וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹלֹ֛ת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד מְלֵאֹ֥ת וְטֹבֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears of grain [were] coming up on one stalk, full and good.

en.L: And I saw in my dream, and look, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and good.
en.B: Then, in my dream, I saw a single stalk with seven ears of grain on it, full and fine.
en.R: Next in my dream I saw one stalk of grain with seven heads on it. They were full and fine.

source.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים צְנֻמ֥וֹת דַּקּ֖וֹת שְׁדֻפ֣וֹת קָדִ֑ים צֹמְח֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, scorched of [the] east wind, [were] sprouting after them.

en.L: And look, seven ears, withered, thin [and] scorched by the east wind, were sprouting up after them.
en.B: Behind them sprang up seven more ears, shriveled, thin and burnt dry by the east wind.
en.R: Then seven more heads of grain grew after them. They were dried up and thin, burned by the hot desert wind.

decisions.choice: withered: shriveled or hardened
decisions.reason: Tsenumot occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. Related words suggest something dried and hardened, so "shriveled" or "withered" is likely.

source.text: וַתִּבְלַ֨עְןָ֙ הָשִׁבֳּלִ֣יםהַדַּקֹּ֔ת אֵ֛ת שֶׁ֥בַע הַֽשִׁבֳּלִ֖ים הַטֹּב֑וֹת וָֽאֹמַר֙ אֶל־הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַגִּ֖יד לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And swallowed the thin ears the seven good ears. And I said to the magicians, and there was none telling to me.

en.L: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears. And I told [it] to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain [it] to me."
en.B: And the thin ears gulped down the seven good ones. I described all this to the magicians, and not one of them could tell me what it meant."
en.R: Then the thin heads ate up the seven good ones. I have told the magicians all this, but they had no explanation for me."

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה חֲל֥וֹם פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶחָ֣ד ה֑וּא אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הִגִּ֥יד לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joseph to Pharaoh, [the] dream of Pharaoh one it [is]; what God is about to do he has told to Pharaoh.

en.L: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has declared to Pharaoh.
en.B: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, "Pharaoh's dreams carry a single message. God has told Pharaoh ahead of time what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going to do.
en.R: Joseph said to Pharaoh, "Your two dreams have one meaning. In them God has shown you what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going to do.

decisions.choice: the dream is one: two dreams, one message
decisions.reason: Pharaoh saw two dreams, but they say one thing. Joseph repeats this (verse 26) and explains why it came twice (verse 32).

decisions.choice: God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do
decisions.reason: The God of Joseph reveals the future to a foreign king, and his own magicians cannot read it. The same pattern returns with Nebuchadnezzar and Daniel (Daniel 2:28).

decisions.choice: you, your
decisions.reason: Readable uses "you" for Pharaoh, as in verse 10; the courtly third person stays at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: שֶׁ֧בַע פָּרֹ֣ת הַטֹּבֹ֗ת שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִים֙ הַטֹּבֹ֔ת שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים הֵ֑נָּה חֲל֖וֹם אֶחָ֥ד הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Seven cows, the good, seven years they [are], and the seven ears, the good, seven years they [are]; [the] dream one it [is].

en.L: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream is one.
en.B: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good ears of grain. It is all one dream.
en.R: The seven good cows mean seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain. The two dreams are really one dream.

source.text: וְשֶׁ֣בַע הַ֠פָּרוֹת הָֽרַקּ֨וֹת וְהָרָעֹ֜ת הָעֹלֹ֣ת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ן שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִׁבֳּלִים֙ הָרֵק֔וֹת שְׁדֻפ֖וֹת הַקָּדִ֑ים יִהְי֕וּ שֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י רָעָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] seven cows, the thin and the bad, coming up after them, seven years they [are], and [the] seven ears, the empty, scorched of the east wind, they will be seven years of famine.

en.L: And the seven thin and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears, scorched by the east wind, will be seven years of famine.
en.B: Likewise the seven scrawny, ugly cows that followed them mean seven years, and the seven empty ears dried out by the east wind mean seven years of famine.
en.R: The seven thin, ugly cows that came up after them are seven more years. So are the seven empty heads of grain dried up by the hot wind. They mean seven years of famine, when there will not be enough food.

decisions.choice: empty: with no grain in them
decisions.reason: Joseph calls the thin ears "empty" (reqot): they look like grain but hold nothing to eat.

decisions.choice: when there will not be enough food
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word famine.

source.text: ה֣וּא הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הֶרְאָ֥ה אֶת־פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: It [is] the word which I spoke to Pharaoh: what God is about to do he has shown Pharaoh.

en.L: This is the thing that I said to Pharaoh: what God is about to do, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown to Pharaoh.
en.B: That is what I told Pharaoh: God has let Pharaoh see in advance what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is about to do.
en.R: So, as I said, God has let you see ahead of time what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} plans to do.

decisions.choice: has shown: the dream as a vision
decisions.reason: In verse 25 God has "told" Pharaoh; here he has "shown" him. A dream is both a message and something seen.

source.text: הִנֵּ֛ה שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים בָּא֑וֹת שָׂבָ֥ע גָּד֖וֹל בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Behold, seven years [are] coming, great plenty in all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: Look, seven years of great plenty are coming in all the land of Egypt.
en.B: Seven years are coming in which all Egypt will have a great abundance.
en.R: For seven years there will be plenty of food all over Egypt.

source.text: וְ֠קָמוּ שֶׁ֜בַעשְׁנֵ֤י רָעָב֙ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן וְנִשְׁכַּ֥ח כָּל־הַשָּׂבָ֖ע בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְכִלָּ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ב אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will arise seven years of famine after them, and will be forgotten all the plenty in [the] land of Egypt, and will consume the famine the land.

en.L: But seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will consume the land.
en.B: But after them will come seven years of famine. People will forget there was ever plenty in Egypt, and the famine will exhaust the land.
en.R: Then seven years of famine will come. People will forget all the good years in Egypt, because the famine will destroy the land.

decisions.choice: the famine will consume the land: use it up, finish it off
decisions.reason: Killah means to bring to an end, to use up completely. The land and its people will be drained of everything.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־יִוָּדַ֤ע הַשָּׂבָע֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֛י הָרָעָ֥ב הַה֖וּא אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֑ן כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד ה֖וּא מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And not will be known the plenty in the land because of that famine after thus, for heavy it [will be] very.

en.L: And the plenty will not be known in the land because of that famine that follows, for it will be very heavy.
en.B: The plenty will not even be noticed in the land, so crushing will the famine be that comes after it.
en.R: The famine that comes next will be so terrible that no one will even remember there was ever plenty of food.

decisions.choice: heavy: severe, hard to bear
decisions.reason: Kaved, "heavy", is used of a famine that weighs on the land (12:10; 43:1; 47:4, 13).

source.text: וְעַ֨ל הִשָּׁנ֧וֹת הַחֲל֛וֹם אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה פַּעֲמָ֑יִם כִּֽי־נָכ֤וֹן הַדָּבָר֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמְמַהֵ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And concerning the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice, it is because established [is] the matter from God, and hurrying [is] God to do it.

en.L: And as for the dream being repeated to Pharaoh twice, [it is] because the matter is established by God, and God is hastening to do it.
en.B: Pharaoh dreamed it twice because God has fixed this in place, and God will waste no time in carrying it out.
en.R: God gave you the same dream two times. That means God has decided this for certain, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make it happen soon.

decisions.choice: repeated twice: the matter is certain
decisions.reason: A double dream confirms that the matter is settled. Joseph's own dreams came in pairs (37:5-9), and so did the dreams in prison (40:5); Scripture also requires two witnesses to establish a matter (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: he
decisions.reason: Readable uses a pronoun for the second mention of God to keep the sentence short.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יֵרֶ֣א פַרְעֹ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ נָב֣וֹן וְחָכָ֑ם וִישִׁיתֵ֖הוּ עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, let see Pharaoh a man discerning and wise, and let him set him over [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: So now let Pharaoh look for a man [who is] discerning and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
en.B: So Pharaoh should now choose someone with understanding and wisdom, and give him authority over the land of Egypt.
en.R: So you should find a man who is wise and understands things well. Make him the one who runs the land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: let Pharaoh see: let him look out, select
decisions.reason: To "see" a person can mean to pick him out (22:8 and 1 Samuel 16:1 use the verb for choosing).

decisions.choice: a man discerning and wise: without knowing it, Joseph describes himself
decisions.reason: Pharaoh takes up these very words in verse 39 and applies them to Joseph.

source.text: יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה פַרְעֹ֔ה וְיַפְקֵ֥ד פְּקִדִ֖ים עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחִמֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י הַשָּׂבָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Let Pharaoh act, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and he will take a fifth of [the] land of Egypt in [the] seven years of the plenty.

en.L: Let Pharaoh do [this]: let him appoint overseers over the land and take a fifth of the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty.
en.B: Pharaoh should act now to place supervisors over the land and collect a fifth of Egypt's harvest during the seven good years.
en.R: You should also choose officers to be in charge of the land. During the seven good years, they should collect one fifth of all the crops in Egypt.

decisions.choice: take a fifth: collect a fifth of the produce
alternatives: organize the land into five districts
decisions.reason: Chimmesh is formed from the word for "five". Joseph proposes collecting a fifth of the harvest, the same share that later became a lasting tax in Egypt (47:24, 26).

decisions.choice: a fifth of Egypt's harvest
alternatives: a fifth of the land of Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "take a fifth of the land of Egypt"; the produce of the land is meant.

source.text: וְיִקְבְּצ֗וּ אֶת־כָּל־אֹ֨כֶל֙ הַשָּׁנִ֣ים הַטֹּבֹ֔ת הַבָּאֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְיִצְבְּרוּ־בָ֞ר תַּ֧חַת יַד־פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֹ֥כֶל בֶּעָרִ֖ים וְשָׁמָֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And let them gather all [the] food of the good years, these coming, and let them heap up grain under [the] hand of Pharaoh, food in the cities, and let them keep [it].

en.L: And let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and store up grain under the hand of Pharaoh, [as] food in the cities, and let them guard [it].
en.B: Let them collect every bit of food from the good years now coming, and stockpile grain in the cities under Pharaoh's control, guarding it as a food supply.
en.R: They should gather food during the good years that are coming. They should store up grain in the cities, under your control, and guard it.

decisions.choice: under the hand of Pharaoh: under his authority
decisions.reason: The "hand" stands for power and control. The grain will be the king's store, held for the country.

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה הָאֹ֤כֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ לְשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹֽא־תִכָּרֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּרָעָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be the food as a reserve for the land for [the] seven years of the famine which will be in [the] land of Egypt, and not will be cut off the land by the famine.

en.L: And the food shall be a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine that will be in the land of Egypt, so that the land will not be cut off by the famine."
en.B: This food will then be a stockpile for the land to draw on during the seven years of famine that Egypt will face, and the land will not be wiped out by the famine."
en.R: That way there will be food saved for the seven hungry years ahead in Egypt. The people in the land will not die from hunger."

decisions.choice: the land will not be cut off: its people will not perish
decisions.reason: "The land" stands for the people who live in it. To be "cut off" is to be destroyed.

decisions.choice: the people in the land
decisions.reason: Readable says who would perish.

source.text: וַיִּיטַ֥ב הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־עֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And was good the word in [the] eyes of Pharaoh and in [the] eyes of all his servants.

en.L: And the proposal was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his officials.
en.B: This advice pleased Pharaoh and all his officials.
en.R: Pharaoh and all his officials thought this was a good plan.

decisions.choice: good in the eyes of: pleasing to
decisions.reason: A common idiom for approval (45:16).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court, his high officials.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־עֲבָדָ֑יו הֲנִמְצָ֣א כָזֶ֔ה אִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֛ר ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Pharaoh to his servants, can we find like this a man in whom [is the] spirit of God?

en.L: And Pharaoh said to his officials, "Can we find [anyone] like this, a man in whom [is] the spirit of God?"
en.B: Pharaoh asked his officials, "Could we ever find another man like this one, a man who has the spirit of God in him?"
en.R: Pharaoh said to his officials, "We could never find a better man than this. The spirit of God is in him."

decisions.choice: the spirit of God: God's power at work in a person
decisions.reason: Elohim can mean God or "gods". From the lips of an Egyptian king it might mean "a divine spirit" (compare Daniel 4:8, 5:11). But Pharaoh is answering Joseph, who has spoken of God throughout, so "the spirit of God" fits the context.

decisions.choice: We could never find a better man than this.
alternatives: Can we find anyone like this?
decisions.reason: Readable turns Pharaoh's question, which expects the answer "no", into a statement.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אַחֲרֵ֨י הוֹדִ֧יעַ אֱלֹהִ֛ים אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶת־כָּל־זֹ֑את אֵין־נָב֥וֹן וְחָכָ֖ם כָּמֽוֹךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, after God has made known to you all this, there is none discerning and wise like you.

en.L: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
en.B: Then Pharaoh turned to Joseph. "God has let you know all of this," he said, "so there is nobody with your insight and wisdom.
en.R: Pharaoh told Joseph, "God has let you know all this. So you are wiser and understand more than anyone else.

decisions.choice: discerning and wise: the words of Joseph's own advice
decisions.reason: Pharaoh repeats the two words Joseph used in verse 33. The man Joseph told him to look for is standing in front of him.

source.text: אַתָּה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה עַל־בֵּיתִ֔י וְעַל־פִּ֖יךָ יִשַּׁ֣ק כָּל־עַמִּ֑י רַ֥ק הַכִּסֵּ֖א אֶגְדַּ֥ל מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: You, you will be over my house, and on your mouth will kiss all my people; only [as to] the throne I will be greater than you.

en.L: You shall be over my house, and all my people shall kiss [in submission] at your word. Only [as to] the throne will I be greater than you."
en.B: You will run my household, and all my people will do as you say. The throne alone will set me above you."
en.R: My palace will be under your control. All my people will follow your orders. Only because I am king will I be above you."

decisions.choice: over my house: in charge of the royal household
decisions.reason: The one "over the house" of a king was his chief steward, a high office (compare Isaiah 22:15, 22). Joseph rose the same way in Potiphar's house (39:4) and in the prison (39:22).

decisions.choice: on your mouth all my people will kiss: they will obey your word
alternatives: all my people will be ruled by your command
all my people will be supplied at your command
decisions.reason: Literally "on your mouth all my people will kiss". Kissing could express homage or submission (Psalm 2:12; 1 Samuel 10:1), and "mouth" stands for a command. The exact sense of the phrase is uncertain, but it plainly gives Joseph authority over the people.

decisions.choice: [in submission]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the sense supplied to the word "kiss".

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי אֹֽתְךָ֔ עַ֖ל כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, see, I have set you over all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt."
en.B: And Pharaoh told Joseph, "Look, I am placing you over all the land of Egypt."
en.R: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Now I am making you ruler over all of Egypt."

decisions.choice: I have set you: done in the saying
decisions.reason: The completed form of the verb makes the appointment take effect as Pharaoh speaks it.

source.text: וַיָּ֨סַר פַּרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־טַבַּעְתּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל יָד֔וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֖הּ עַל־יַ֣ד יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיַּלְבֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ בִּגְדֵי־שֵׁ֔שׁ וַיָּ֛שֶׂם רְבִ֥ד הַזָּהָ֖ב עַל־צַוָּארֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And removed Pharaoh his signet ring from on his hand and put it on [the] hand of Joseph, and clothed him [in] garments of fine linen and put the chain of gold on his neck.

en.L: Then Pharaoh took his signet ring off his hand and put it on Joseph's hand, and he clothed him [in] garments of fine linen and put the gold chain on his neck.
en.B: Pharaoh slipped the signet ring off his hand and placed it on Joseph's. He had him dressed in clothes of fine linen and hung a gold chain on his neck.
en.R: Pharaoh took off his own ring with the royal seal and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave Joseph fine linen clothes to wear and a gold chain to hang around his neck.

decisions.choice: signet ring: the king's seal
decisions.reason: A signet ring was pressed into clay or wax to seal documents. Whoever held the king's ring could act in his name (Esther 3:10; 8:2).

decisions.choice: fine linen and a gold chain: the dress of a high Egyptian official
decisions.reason: Shesh is fine Egyptian linen, worn by priests and nobles. A gold collar or chain was a royal honor given to high officers. Joseph, stripped of his robe by his brothers (37:23) and of his garment by Potiphar's wife (39:12), is now dressed by the king.

decisions.choice: ring with the royal seal
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a signet ring was.

source.text: וַיַּרְכֵּ֣ב אֹת֗וֹ בְּמִרְכֶּ֤בֶת הַמִּשְׁנֶה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ לְפָנָ֖יו אַבְרֵ֑ךְ וְנָת֣וֹן אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ל כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made him ride in [the] chariot of the second [rank] which [was] to him, and they called out before him, Abrek! And setting him over all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And he had him ride in his second chariot, and they called out before him, "Abrek!" So he set him over all the land of Egypt.
en.B: He let him ride in the chariot that was second only to his own, and men called out ahead of him, "Bow down!" In this way Pharaoh set him over the entire land of Egypt.
en.R: Joseph rode in the chariot of the king's second-in-command. Men in front of him shouted, "Bow down!" So Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over all of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the chariot of the second: the chariot of the second-ranking man
decisions.reason: Mishneh means "second". The chariot belongs to the one second in rank after the king, or it is the king's second chariot; either way it marks Joseph as the second man in Egypt.

decisions.choice: Abrek: an unclear cry, perhaps "Bow down!"
decisions.reason: Abrek occurs only here. It sounds like a form of the Hebrew barak, "kneel", which fits a herald's cry to bow. It may also be a word borrowed from Egyptian meaning "Attention!" or "Make way!". The meaning is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Bow down!
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable translate the cry by its likely sense; Literal keeps the word as it stands.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף אֲנִ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וּבִלְעָדֶ֗יךָ לֹֽא־יָרִ֨ים אִ֧ישׁ אֶת־יָד֛וֹ וְאֶת־רַגְל֖וֹ בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, I [am] Pharaoh, and apart from you not will lift a man his hand and his foot in all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, and without you no one shall lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt."
en.B: "I am Pharaoh," he told Joseph, "and yet no one anywhere in Egypt will so much as move a hand or a foot unless you allow it."
en.R: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am the king. But no one in all of Egypt will do anything unless you say so."

decisions.choice: I am Pharaoh: the king's own word stands behind the grant
decisions.reason: Pharaoh names himself to seal what he grants. Joseph's authority rests on the king's authority.

decisions.choice: lift hand or foot: do anything at all
decisions.reason: To lift neither hand nor foot is to make no move. Nothing will happen in Egypt without Joseph's permission.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֣ה שֵׁם־יוֹסֵף֮ צָֽפְנַ֣ת פַּעְנֵחַ֒ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֣וֹ אֶת־אָֽסְנַ֗ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֛רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֹ֖ן לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֖ף עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Pharaoh [the] name of Joseph Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave to him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as wife. And went out Joseph over [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as a wife. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
en.B: Pharaoh renamed Joseph Zaphenath-paneah and married him to Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. And Joseph went out to take charge of the land of Egypt.
en.R: Pharaoh gave Joseph an Egyptian name, Zaphenath-paneah. He also gave him a wife, Asenath. She was the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of On. Then Joseph went out to rule over Egypt.

decisions.choice: Zaphenath-paneah: an Egyptian name
decisions.reason: The name is Egyptian, probably meaning something like "God speaks and he lives" or "the one who gives life". An old explanation reads it as "revealer of secrets". A new name marked Joseph as a member of the Egyptian court (compare Daniel 1:7).

decisions.choice: Potiphera, priest of On: a leading priestly family
decisions.reason: On, later called Heliopolis, north of modern Cairo, was a center of the worship of the sun god Ra. Potiphera probably means "the one whom Ra gave", a fuller form of Potiphar (37:36). Marriage into this family gave Joseph high standing.

decisions.choice: went out over the land: took up his office throughout Egypt
decisions.reason: "Went out over" describes Joseph setting out in his new authority; verse 46 says he traveled through the whole country.

source.text: וְיוֹסֵף֙ בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעָמְד֕וֹ לִפְנֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיַּעְבֹ֖רבְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joseph [was] a son of thirty years when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And went out Joseph from before Pharaoh and passed through all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: Now Joseph [was] thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh and passed through all the land of Egypt.
en.B: Joseph was thirty years old when he took up his post before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Leaving the king's presence, Joseph made a tour of the whole land of Egypt.
en.R: Joseph was thirty years old when he went to work for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. He left the palace and went on a journey through the whole country.

decisions.choice: stood before Pharaoh: entered his service
decisions.reason: To "stand before" a king is to serve him as an officer (1 Samuel 16:21; 1 Kings 12:8).

decisions.choice: thirty years old: thirteen years after he was sold
decisions.reason: Joseph was seventeen when his brothers sold him (37:2). Thirteen years of slavery and prison lie behind him.

source.text: וַתַּ֣עַשׂ הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֣י הַשָּׂבָ֑ע לִקְמָצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And produced the land in [the] seven years of the plenty by handfuls.

en.L: And in the seven years of plenty the land produced by handfuls.
en.B: In the seven years of plenty the land produced heaping handfuls.
en.R: During the seven good years, the land grew huge crops.

decisions.choice: by handfuls: in abundance
decisions.reason: Qematsim are handfuls. The land produced so much that it could be gathered by the handful.

source.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֞ץ אֶת־כָּל־אֹ֣כֶל׀שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּתֶּן־אֹ֖כֶל בֶּעָרִ֑ים אֹ֧כֶל שְׂדֵה־הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְבִיבֹתֶ֖יהָ נָתַ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gathered all [the] food of [the] seven years which were in [the] land of Egypt and put food in the cities; [the] food of [the] field of the city which [was] around it he put in its midst.

en.L: And he gathered all the food of the seven years that were in the land of Egypt and put the food in the cities. The food from the fields around each city he put in it.
en.B: Throughout those seven years in Egypt Joseph gathered up all the food and laid it up in the cities. Every city received the food from its own surrounding fields.
en.R: Joseph gathered all the food that grew in Egypt during those seven years. He stored it in the cities. Each city kept the food from the farms around it.

decisions.choice: the seven years: the Hebrew text
alternatives: the seven years of plenty (Samaritan Pentateuch, Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient Greek translation read "the seven years of plenty", which is the plain sense of the Hebrew in any case. The Hebrew text is followed here.

source.text: וַיִּצְבֹּ֨ר יוֹסֵ֥ף בָּ֛ר כְּח֥וֹל הַיָּ֖ם הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד עַ֛ד כִּי־חָדַ֥ל לִסְפֹּ֖ר כִּי־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And heaped up Joseph grain like [the] sand of the sea, very much, until he ceased to count, for there was no number.

en.L: And Joseph heaped up grain like the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting [it], for it was beyond number.
en.B: Joseph amassed grain in huge quantities, as plentiful as the sand by the sea. In the end he gave up counting it, for there was too much to count.
en.R: Joseph piled up grain like sand on the beach. There was so much of it that at last he gave up counting. No one could measure it all.

decisions.choice: like the sand of the sea: beyond counting
decisions.reason: The same picture describes the descendants God promised Abraham and Jacob (22:17; 32:12). The abundance that saves many lives comes through Abraham's line.

source.text: וּלְיוֹסֵ֤ף יֻלַּד֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא שְׁנַ֣ת הָרָעָ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Joseph were born two sons before came [the] year of the famine, whom bore to him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.

en.L: And to Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
en.B: Two sons were born to Joseph before the first year of famine came. Their mother was Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
en.R: Before the famine started, Joseph and his wife Asenath had two sons. Asenath was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם הַבְּכ֖וֹר מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה כִּֽי־נַשַּׁ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־כָּל־עֲמָלִ֔י וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Joseph [the] name of the firstborn Manasseh, for has made me forget God all my trouble and all [the] house of my father.

en.L: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, "For God has made me forget all my trouble and all my father's house."
en.B: Joseph called his firstborn son Manasseh, "because," he said, "God has let me forget all my hardship and my father's whole household."
en.R: Joseph named his first son Manasseh, which means "making forget." He said, "God has helped me forget all my hard times, and my father's family too."

decisions.choice: Manasseh: "making forget"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like nashshani, "he has made me forget". The pain of the past no longer rules Joseph's life.

decisions.choice: forget my father's house: the grief is healed, not the memory erased
decisions.reason: Joseph has not literally forgotten his family; when his brothers arrive he remembers his dreams at once (42:9). God has eased the ache of losing them.

decisions.choice: which means "making forget"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name so the reason given makes sense (m1).

source.text: וְאֵ֛ת שֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י קָרָ֣א אֶפְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־הִפְרַ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ עָנְיִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of the second he called Ephraim, for has made me fruitful God in [the] land of my affliction.

en.L: And the name of the second he called Ephraim, "For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."
en.B: The second son he called Ephraim, "because," he said, "God has made me fruitful in the country where I was afflicted."
en.R: He named his second son Ephraim, which means "fruitful." He said, "God has given me children in the land where I suffered so much."

decisions.choice: Ephraim: "fruitful"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like hiprani, "he has made me fruitful", from the verb parah. Its ending may suggest "doubly fruitful".

decisions.choice: made me fruitful: God's blessing on Abraham's family
decisions.reason: "Be fruitful" was God's blessing at creation (1:28) and his promise to Abraham and Jacob (17:6; 35:11). It comes true for Joseph in the land of his suffering.

decisions.choice: which means "fruitful"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name.

decisions.choice: has given me children
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being fruitful means here.

source.text: וַתִּכְלֶ֕ינָה שֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֣י הַשָּׂבָ֑ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came to an end [the] seven years of the plenty which was in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And the seven years of plenty that had been in the land of Egypt came to an end,
en.B: The seven years of plenty that Egypt had enjoyed came to an end.
en.R: Then the seven good years in Egypt ended.

source.text: וַתְּחִלֶּ֜ינָה שֶׁ֣בַע שְׁנֵ֤י הָרָעָב֙ לָב֔וֹא כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בְּכָל־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת וּבְכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם הָ֥יָה לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And began [the] seven years of the famine to come, just as had said Joseph. And there was famine in all the lands, but in all [the] land of Egypt there was bread.

en.L: and the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. And there was famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
en.B: Then the seven years of famine set in, as Joseph had said they would. Famine struck every land around, yet all over Egypt people still had food.
en.R: The seven years of famine started, as Joseph had said. People in all the other countries were going hungry, but in Egypt there was food to eat.

decisions.choice: bread: food in general
decisions.reason: Lechem, "bread", often stands for food of every kind.

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "food", the sense of the word here.

source.text: וַתִּרְעַב֙ כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֛ם אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה לַלָּ֑חֶם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֤ה לְכָל־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לְכ֣וּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמַ֥ר לָכֶ֖ם תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was hungry all [the] land of Egypt, and cried out the people to Pharaoh for bread. And said Pharaoh to all Egypt, go to Joseph; what he says to you, do.

en.L: When all the land of Egypt was hungry, the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all Egypt, "Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do."
en.B: Before long the whole land of Egypt felt the hunger too, and the people appealed to Pharaoh for food. Pharaoh's answer to all Egypt was, "Go to Joseph. Whatever he tells you, do it."
en.R: When the people of Egypt also began to go hungry, they begged Pharaoh for food. Pharaoh told them all, "Go to Joseph, and do what he says."

decisions.choice: all the land of Egypt was hungry: when its own harvests failed
decisions.reason: Egypt had stored grain (verse 54), but as the famine went on the people's own supplies ran out and they turned to the king.

decisions.choice: whatever he tells you, do it
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's words to the hungry people are echoed by Jesus' mother at Cana: "Do whatever he tells you" (John 2:5).

source.text: וְהָרָעָ֣ב הָיָ֔ה עַ֖ל כָּל־פְּנֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶֽת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֣ר לְמִצְרַ֔יִם וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָֽרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the famine was over all [the] face of the land, and opened Joseph all that [was] in them, and he sold grain to Egypt; and was severe the famine in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And the famine was over all the face of the land, and Joseph opened all that had [grain] in it, and he sold grain to the Egyptians. And the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
en.B: The famine covered the whole face of the land. Joseph threw open every place where grain was stored and began selling it to the Egyptians, and the famine kept its hard grip on Egypt.
en.R: The famine spread across the whole country. Joseph opened up the storehouses and began selling grain to the people of Egypt. Things were very bad in Egypt because of the famine.

decisions.choice: all that was in them: the storehouses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "all that was in them", meaning the stores in the cities (verse 48). The ancient Greek translation says "all the granaries", which gives the sense.

decisions.choice: sold grain: shavar, trade in grain
decisions.reason: Shavar is the word for grain as a ration and for trading in it, buying (42:2-3) or, as here, selling. Joseph does not give the grain away; he sells it.

decisions.choice: every place where grain was stored / the storehouses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the storehouses to be understood from verse 48.

source.text: וְכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ בָּ֣אוּ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה לִשְׁבֹּ֖ר אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the earth came to Egypt to buy grain, to Joseph, for severe was the famine in all the earth.

en.L: And all the earth came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
en.B: The whole world came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, since the famine had tightened its hold everywhere on earth.
en.R: From every country people traveled to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine had hit the whole world hard.

decisions.choice: all the earth: people from every land
decisions.reason: "The earth" stands for its people, here the peoples of the lands around Egypt, among them Jacob's family (42:1).

decisions.choice: to Joseph: the nations come for food to Abraham's descendant
decisions.reason: God promised that through Abraham all the families of the earth would be blessed (12:3). Here the whole world comes to Abraham's great-grandson for bread.
